description.purpose: A script a manifest can name, as one `code` cell shipped BLANK: a runner, a timeout and a pass-through, and nothing else. It exists because the five shipped templates that hold a single `code` cell each carry a script and a purpose of their own, so a composer that needed a plain one had nothing to name and spent seven rounds looking (GH #482). It runs, it decides nothing: WHAT it does is the `script_inline` the declaration hands it.
description.use_when: Wherever a topology needs application logic between two cells -- reshaping a body, extracting the calls out of an answer, turning one message into several. Instantiate it under a name that says what it does, hand it its script in the SAME declaration as `override_params` (a FLAT params object here, because a single-cell template has no inner cell to address), and draw the edges around it.
description.not_in_scope: No state: a `code` cell has no `cell.db`, so anything that must outlive a message goes to a store over the topology. No sandbox either -- a cell instantiated without the key gets the default-deny profile, and this template does not declare the key, so no manifest can widen it through here. And no free lunch: an `override_params` that carries a `script_inline` is EXECUTABLE BEHAVIOUR arriving with a manifest, which is the `code.author` question the submitter asks its colony, disabled by default -- a refusal is `code_author_denied` and means THIS COLONY DOES NOT ALLOW IMPORTED EXECUTION, never that the manifest was malformed.
examples: PORTS - Entry: any message; the shipped script reads `body.messages` and hands it straight back. Exit: one message per content json the script writes (SCRIPT, below) -- an object is one, an ARRAY one per element because `multi_send_capable` is declared here, each evaluated against this cell's edges independently. The cell stamps `exit_code`, `duration_ms` and `had_stderr` on the hop and a script cannot hijack them.

SCRIPT - stdin is ONE json doc of THREE objects (`envelope`, `body`, `params`): the payload is `doc["body"]["messages"]`, and a turn carries `text`, never `turns`. `hop` and `context` sit in `doc["envelope"]["header"]`, never at `envelope["context"]`. stdout is ONE content json of BODY SLOTS -- `messages` plus an optional `header` the colony reads as `hop`; a `{"content": ...}` is not a body slot and comes back `contract_violation`. PASS-THROUGH:
```
import sys, json
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
print(json.dumps({"messages": doc["body"]["messages"]}))
```
TRANSFORM:
```
import sys, json
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
args = json.dumps({"url": doc["body"]["messages"][-1]["text"]})
call = {"origin": "assistant", "type": "tool_call", "id": "q1", "text": args}
print(json.dumps({"header": {"route": "fetch"}, "messages": [call]}))
```

one document per new item: { "add_nodes": [{"name": "dedupe", "template": "scriptlet", "override_params": {"script_inline": "..."}}], "add_edges": [{"from": "./dedupe", "to": "./headlines", "condition": "has(hop.route) && hop.route == 'store'"}] }
